Title: Oh no! Not the Succubus Club!

Messages.Author: Legendre
Messages.Body: MY GOD! The whining.... Look, if you think that your prey is going to use Succubus Club in a snit to give all his stuff and pool to /his/ prey (or your predator), well then you've got to make sure he doesn't do that. "Gee Mike... how do we do that?" Well, you can start by not backing your prey into a corner, not giving him a reason to screw you over. Ease up. Give him some breathing room and a chance to live. Don't drop the hammer until you're ready to finish him. Hope is a dangerous weapon. Use it. Adapt. Smile. Be subtle. Or, if you prefer the brute force approach, you could try one of my favourite cards: Political Flux. Give yourself twelve pool and LET him give away all his stuff. "But Mike... Succubus Club allows the boogeyman [kingmaking!] into our games!" Fer christ's sake, go ahead and let someone be the "kingmaker"... then kill their f***ing king. Get allies of your own. What? No one wants to be your friend because you're playing a stealth bleed deck that doesn't do anything but kill people? Well isn't that too f***ing bad. Play a more flexible deck next time, you lop! You're supposed to be JYHAD PLAYERS, ancient bad-ass vampires, not some pansy-a** network of Mary Kay marketers worrying about infringing on each other's customers and territories. What's that? You don't like any of these ideas? Well how about trying to take control of the Succubus Club yourself? Someone mentioned packing a few to contest it... or maybe including some disputed territories or arsons. You don't like the effect the Succubus Club is having on your game? You don't like your prey having leverage on you? BURN THE F***ING THING TO THE GROUND. That's the spirit! That's a Methuselah who comes ready to fight. That's a player I can respect. -Michael

Succubus club can be nasty, I certainly agree.

However, in effect it's (merely?) an amplifier of the possible ways of
dealing that exist between methuselahs. I've been in plenty of games
(and recently, the amount has grown) where deals take place - they can
be disturbing enough even without the succubus club. I'm just saying
this to illustrate that even without succubus club, the behaviour we
dislike would take place anyway.

However, probably in a less-disturbing manner than is possible with
the succubus club. With the succubus club, much broader deal-making
becomes possible, so much more profound deals are possible. And since
it's very likely only one part of a deal-making alliance will be
having access to the effects of the SC, this further decreases the
natural balance between competing alliances.

So, I wouldn't mind it if the SC were disallowed in V:EKN tournaments.
But I'm not raving for it either, since the disturbing nature of the
deals might better be tackled at the 'root' than at the SC.

--

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
Tobias wrote:

> However, in effect it's (merely?) an amplifier of the possible ways of
> dealing that exist between methuselahs.

The amplification is what makes the card so disruptive. Without the Succubus
Club, deals are generally vague, as there is only so much you can do that is
concrete--help out with a vote in exchange for some favorible KRC damage;
call a Con Boon for my clan in exchange for a Rush; block that action and
I'll let you steal the Powerbase; whatever. It is difficult to make a very
significant deal, as the rules lack an inherrent mechanism to make them
concrete. Thus, in most cases, deals in VTES are going to be fairly vague.

Throw in the SC, and suddenly, you have the capability of making very
significant concrete deals, and when these deals turn out to be one sided
for whatever reason, they tend to throw the game.

Yeah, a mundane, balanced trade with the SC isn't going to be that damaging
to anything, but having your prey suddenly inherrit 3 vampires, 6 pool, a
VP, and then 6 more pool 'cause his prey decided he wanted out of the game
and wanted to spite you for not voting in favor of a vote of his earlier in
the game is just ass.

> I'm just saying
> this to illustrate that even without succubus club, the behaviour we
> dislike would take place anyway.

Yes. But it would be much less concrete. And wouldn't include giving all of
your stuff and pool to your predator 'cause you are in a losing position and
filled with spite. Or 'cause you are in a losing position, and your predator
is a pal who you'd be happy to win the tournament if you can't.

> So, I wouldn't mind it if the SC were disallowed in V:EKN tournaments.
> But I'm not raving for it either, since the disturbing nature of the
> deals might better be tackled at the 'root' than at the SC.

You can't really fix the root problem (deal making), except in the most
vague sense--and they already have done so for what it is worth (VEKN
tournament rules 5.1 and 5.2), but these rules simply call for too much
taxation on the judges to arbitrate every possible deal situation.

Succubus Club aggrivates the "deal making" problem (which is enough of a
problem to have called for the VEKN rules as well as the move towards "table
wins" as opposed to just VPs so as to dis-incentive table splits) to a great
deal. Yeah, it can be used for mundane, reasonable trades, but as LSJ
pointed out, you can't really invent strict limits that will prevent
unreasonable trades (yeah, I can only give you a maximum of 2 pool, but then
I can give you 1 pool for your Arika with a Flamethrower...). Leading back
to the need to have a judge arbitrate every deal made with the Succubus
Club. Which is a pain in the ass.

The reasonable uses of the Succubus Club simply do not justfy the huge
amounts of damage the card can cause.

Your angst, your futility, the absolute *HORROR* of what has happened

all that it engenders, which I shall never understand or comprehend
because in all my VTES playing years I've only participated in three

tournament twice and once by *me* filthy little collusive Jyhad Slut
that I am, does nonetheless and despite my obvious flaws reveal one,
or perhaps three, things which I believe I can state with near
certainty:

1) You have forgotten that this is a game.

2) You think this VTES thing really matters.

3) You have forgotten that it is supposed to be *FUN*.

I myself do not claim to be "macho" or anything. I simply know that
when I'm playing VTES I play to win, even if the whole table is
arrayed against me. I /despise/ the tournament rules on "having" to
play to maximize VPs. What else is there? And who cares if someone
else decides to collude or kingmake or wear plaid with paisley? So
long as they've got a deck and are ready to roll. If you don't think
that you can subvert or evade the effects of the Succubus Club, then
take it as flattery that your prey felt he had no option but to
suicide and take you with him. Think of it like a "poison pill" in
Mergers & Acquisitions. It's a fact of life. Accept it. Play as
hard and fast as you can. Adapt and overcome your enemies, or be
crushed underfoot. Those are really the only two options in a game
like this. But if you must pass beyond the veil of ouster, do try to
transubstantiate with style and grace.

When the tournament is over, when your cards lay burned and your pool
expended, enjoy the satisfaction of knowing that you gave it your
best, that you built a good deck and it just wasn't good enough to
take everyone out. You had fun playing a game. Hell, you might even
have gotten a victory point from your prey's actions if you put any
defense in your deck whatsoever!

And then you go back to your job, your house, your wife or husband or
fiancee or girlfriend or boyfriend or children, your other hobbies,
your books, your music, your favourite movies, and life is *good*
because you had fun playing a game and even though you lost, the
Succubus Club made things more interesting. Maybe next time you'll
try something insane like offering to help your prey kill your
grandprey in order to keep him from going postal. Or maybe next time
you'll play something that makes it so your prey has no minions to
give away. Whatever. It's a game. Life is good, wine is good, and
writing poetry is good. Whatever floats your particular little
private boat is *good*, and you went out and gave it your best.

Or, or more likely it seems, you sit around whining about how that
bastard gave all his minions away and he shouldn't be allowed to do
that because it's collusion and they might be friend and and how a
perfectly wonderful game needs to ban one of the most interesting,
useful cards in the set and how the game needs yet more restrictive
rules to prevent players from playing their games how they want to
because even though the rules say you can earn your zero VPs any way
you want they can't really mean it and someone should do something
there ought to be a LAW!

As I said before, it's your perogative.

-Michael

their way to limit the interaction of (see: predator/prey relationship;
blocking of (D) actions; default bleed actions; blocking of non (D) actions;
etc.). The game benefits greatly by this inherrent limit. Succubus Club

intentions to impact the game.

specifically named as cheating.

> and start making judgements about certain cards or even MECHANICS and

given game for some reason other than the stated goal of the game (getting
the most VPs at the table).

> as a gameplay element.

Possibly. But I know me, and I know Derek. And this is clearly not a factor
in either of our arguments (or personalities). Yet here we are.

Well, given that the suggestion was "you can use the Succubus Club
only if you control the edge", I don't think that Derek's point was
wrong. Currently, you can only use the SC during the start of your
turn (i.e. before you take actions, and thus before you can get the
edge). Thus, given the suggestion, to use the SC, you'd need to have
the edge at the start of your turn. As the control of the edge is
passed by virtue of the actions of the other 4 players at the table,
most of which you have zero control over, the ability to have the edge
at the start of a given turn (so as to facilitate the use of the
Succubus Club)is essentially random (unless you are playing a Madness
Network deck or a "20 Eagle's Sight" deck...). Thus, the SC becomes
mostly worthless.

If the suggestion had included something along the lines of "you can
tap the SC whenever you want, but you must have the edge", that'd be a
different discussion all together.

ability to make deals and manage the table, 'prodigious' both due to
the political nature of his deck and also Vince's personal negotiating
prowess. In the game I played it sort of did that, and also sort of
serviced spite. I'm not sure how great an 'abuse' his use was, but it
certainly sucked wazoo to be on the receiving end of it, and there was
little I could do about it at the point it became an issue.

The table was Vince preying on Chuck (ani, pot, vic, Sabbat toolboxy
guys with significant combat, some intercept, some rush, some bleed)
preying on me (pot, tha, vic, Sabbat rush-monkeys) preying on Kai
(ani, chi, pro, Camarilla chi/Prince intercepty stuff? - Man did he
regret putting Tension down...). The dynamic pretty much broke down
to me wiping the floor with Kai (and rescuing a fair amount when
poked) while Chuck tried vainly to fend off Vince's ever increasing
horde.

Early on I drew my Rampage and used it to burn down Kai's Heidelberg
Castle so he'd stop rearraging all his blood. Later, Vince played the
Succubus Club; I pointed out that we should all now try to kill him.
Unfortunately I didn't take my own advice. (As Kai was his predator
and Chuck his prey was already trying to kill him, it was really just
me who should have started going cross-table.)

Soon thereafter I was the recipient of a cross-table Parity Shift for
4 (My first of two cross-table Parity Shifts on the day - one per
game!); this was good play on Vince's part, as it made it that more
imperative that I oust my prey quickly and not mess around with him
cross-table. It still sucked.

At this point the Succubus Club started to factor in. Kai was on the
ropes, with me repeatedly putting his vampires down, so he started
dealing with Vince, trading cards (Judgement: Camarilla Segregation
to Vince, the Millicent on Vince to Kai) for pool. This didn't help
Kai to win, but did maintain him as a meat shield. Without Fame
dunkage they probably could have kept it up for quite some time, to
say nothing of the potential for Kai to dump his (torped) minions, pro
cards, and remaining pool to Vince had they really wanted to go the
total sleaze route.

A Fame dunk and a bleed or two got Kai anyway, but between the Parity
Shift and the extra actions I was too weak for Vince as he plowed
through Chuck and then finished me off in a couple turns.

Like I say, it was all solid play on Vince's part, and not really
'abuse' per se of Succubus Club, but a) a little more spite would've
probably have pushed it into the 'abuse' category in my mind, and
there was nothing to stop that, and b) even without 'abuse' it still
had an awfully powerful effect on the game, and could potentially have
had an even greater one. My only potential for response was to go
cross-table early and often, so the whole predator/prey dynamic was
(or should have been) thrown out the window.

Anyway, I guess my main point, other than to just contribute an
example from real life, is that... Parity Shift should be banned.
Dammit. (And that I should consider going cross-table more often.)

Tajdid is probably not a good analogy, since it's not even all that
powerful an effect. I think it's a "once per game" card because (a)
once one is played, another wouldn't do anything useful anyway, (b) for
backstory/flavor reasons, and (c) so that an Assamite deck can't pack
*too* many of them to make sure of drawing them early (without risking
hand-jamming on them later).

Giant's Blood is a better example, because it's a very powerful card
even with the "once per game" restriction. I would say that Giant's
Blood actually is in the "close to overpowered" zone even though it's
only playable once per game. It would be absurdly powerful if playable
again and again. It may actually have been a poor design choice to make
it as is, because there *is* quite a bit of luck involved in who gets to
draw their Giant's Blood first and gain the benefit of refilling a large
vampire for free, when multiple people have Giant's Blood in their deck
(as is fairly common around DC these days).

Ancient Influence, Political Stranglehold, Reins of Power, and Dia de
los Muertos all use the same mechanic, and are also pretty powerful
effects even at "once per game". They don't provide *quite* as much of
a swing as Giant's Blood, though (except for DdlMuertos, which might
sometimes), so they're probably more or less OK.

On the whole, the "once per game" limitation is a dangerous tool in my
opinion. It can be used to "balance" cards, but you still have to be
pretty careful that the effect doesn't remain "broken" even if it only
happens once. It is very possible for that to be the case. As such, I
don't think even a "trade once per game" limitation on Succubus Club
would be an especially appropriate way to "fix" it, since it would still
be possible for games to be "thrown" via SC that way. If you're going
to neuter or nearly neuter a card, it may be that you might as well just
ban it instead (see Return to Innocence for an example of a card that
this happened to).

Bribes is more reliable, but the theoretical Succubus Club would be far more
flexible. Trading cards out of hand is a mechanic that there is zero way to
do otherwise. Sure, it might not be all that useful on a regular basis, but
it would still be a unique, flexible effect that someone would build a deck
around. Trading cards in hand could be very helpful in many situations and
is something that all deck types could, theoretically, benefit from. And it
could still be used for deal making/bribery/hired hits if someone wanted
too.

Heck. Play some sort of kooky Ian Forrestal multi-rush deck. Trade hits for
stuff you want out of your hand in exchange for good bleed modifiers ("I'll
kill Arika if you give me a Conditioning or something in exchange for this
third Bum's Rush card..."). Play a vote deck with a bunch of random weird
but valuable cards that you can't necessarily use that you plan on trading
off for favors. There are plenty of kooky tricks you could pull off with the
theoretically restricted Succubus Club if you put your mind to it. Would it
be an auto include in any deck, just to have significant leverage? No, but
it would be clever and kinda fun. And possibly fairly useful in the right
circumstances.

Sure, only being able to trade cards in hand is much less useful, in an
absolute sense, that being able to trade anything and everything, but if
Succubus Club was restricted to only trading cards in hand from day one, I'm
sure it would have shown up occasionally, and still would have been used for
clever game winning manuvers sometimes. It just seems super sucky compared
to what Succubus Club is now. Which it is, but that's ok.

Further, the definition of Game Theory is defined as follows (see:

A branch of mathematics and logic which deals with the analysis of
games (i.e., situations involving parties with conflicting interests).
In addition to the mathematical elegance and complete "solution" which
is possible for simple games, the principles of game theory also find
applications to complicated games such as cards, checkers, and chess,

object of VTES, the game in question, is. From the rules:
Object of the Game

Your goal is to accumulate the most victory points by destroying the
influence held by rival Methuselahs.

Pretty simple.

It's not quite a Zero Sum Game because of the total number of counters

isn't necessarily the winner. It's more of a variation on both,
probably best called an Attrition Game, wherein the total amount of
"money" (overall) and players approaches zero as the game continues.

socialize." You can do that, sure. But that is not the object of the
game being played. If you're not attempting to reach that goal, you're

have to actually be in your HAND to be used in this fashion, leaving you
at the mercy of your shuffle.

Removing the ability to trade pool means that the Succubus Club can no
longer be used as an "extortion" or "bounty" tactic, both of which are
clever, innovative uses. So I don't like touching that. Reducing the
amount of pool traded to "no more than 2" sounds good at first, but what
about a bloat deck that wants to buy its way to victory, and would like
to spend 4-6 pool for a minion with a bunch of equipment? ... buying,
of course, from a person who is close to being ousted and has plenty of
minions?

Removing the ability to trade cards in play removes the ability to hand
over Hunting Grounds, ANY location, you name it. It also removes the
ability to pass guns or laptops around for, say, pool cost +1? Again,
it excessively restricts "good" uses of the Club.

So I don't see what can properly be restricted without just making the
card pointless to play. Ideas welcome, but...

Babylon 5 had as one of its official formats, actually pretty much second to
constructed, "social tournaments". You got points for telling the best story
and making the game the most fun. For quite a few people, the proper way to
play this format was to let people do whatever inane things they wanted to do
with the cards in the name of playing a "fun" game, such things as spelling
words with card titles and the like. In fact, because winning ended the game
before people could do whatever they wanted, winning was antifun and would
likely cause you to score worse. One might find it hard to believe how much
resistance there was to my point that if you don't try to stop someone from
doing something then it doesn't matter what that someone does. I offered as a
hypothetical social goal successfully passing 1000 times in a row before the
game ended (i.e. doing nothing all game). In what way was allowing someone to
do what that person wanted any more valid than letting someone spend the entire
game doing nothing? Lot of people I dealt with never seemed to grasp the
point.

This was extreme(ly stupid). More subtle, though rather common in CCGdom, is
peer pressuring out certain archetypes because they are considered unfun, e.g.
weenie decks in V:TES. Not a problem when everyone plays by the unwritten
rules. What if you don't know what the unwritten rules are? What if you don't
care?

The reality is that you will produce more unpleasantness by trying to have
people conform to unwritten rules than by having people play to achieve the
goals set out by the game.

If the game has glaring flaws in terms of fundamentals, card base, card
combinations, then it's better that everyone know about them and get the game
changed than to try to work around them. The flaws only become obvious when
people analyze what wins in a crossregional environment or an environment that
simulates such.
